chapter: Wartime South and the Ernie Fields band
title: Wat Sanders' Blue Room in Tampa and pianist Chick Stephens
summary: The band takes a Tampa job where he meets Art Tatum-class pianist Chick Stephens.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: And Bolden was drafted. So they decided to make me the leader. I was voted the leader of the band! So we stayed there, and played until we were approached about another job in Tampa, Florida, at a place called Wat Sanders' Blue Room -- the Blue Room, and Wat Sanders was the guy who owned it. And so we decided to take it. So we went down there, and I stayed down there for about three months. And I had a great time. In fact, that's where I met one of the great pianists, one of the greatest pianists you would ever hear. It was fantastic that this guy never really got known, because he was like in the Art Tatum class of piano playing. In fact, when Jimmie Lunceford came through and played the dance at the place where we were working, the guys in the band, they could hardly wait to play intermission so they could hear him play the piano. His name was Chick Stephens. They called him Abba-Dabba. A fantastic pianist, and great
writer -- and a very, very nice man.
